pr.body:
## Purpose

This is our **draft reference implementation of [RFC #57103: Programmable KV Cache](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57103)**, shared for design discussion and implementation review. It does not close the RFC or claim complete acceptance.

Agentic sessions span multiple inference requests, tool pauses, and branches. The RFC lets an application express lifecycle and cache intent through the existing `KvHintsEnvelope`, while the engine resolves targets, approves resources, executes operations, and reports actual completion.

### How this implementation maps to the RFC

- **Common control and logical state:** request-attached hints and independent Python/HTTP control share the envelope, dispatcher, and engine approval path. Hash/session/continuation/range selectors resolve logical content separately from physical residency. Results are correlated by message/action IDs, with bounded replay, queries, ACK, cancellation, and engine epochs. Existing backend-owned KVCR payloads retain opaque forwarding.
- **Execution through existing cache infrastructure:** `SET_PRIORITY`, `COPY_TO`, and `MOVE_TO` use `KVCacheManager`/`BlockPool` and CPU/Mooncake Store adapters. GPU-source operations run at successful request completion before references are released; accepted transfers can outlive the request. COPY publishes reusable GPU content only after all participating ranks finish. MOVE stores first and reclaims eligible source copies afterward. Shared loads share reservations and transfer holds; a resume can wait for an existing load.
- **Optional policies and rollout integration:** retention, tool-wait movement, and quota/prefix-reuse scheduling consume engine observations and submit proposals through the same approval boundary. Explicit commands keep their meaning. Startup configuration controls policy registration. The benchmark harness connects real verl `ToolAgentLoop` calls, tools, token logprobs, response masks, and rewards; weight-update checks exercise draining, invalidation, and cache namespace isolation.

Implementation contracts: [native primitives and lifecycle](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/vllm/v1/kv_hints/README.md). Reproduction: [benchmark commands](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/benchmarks/programmable_kv_cache/README.md).

### Current conclusions

Recorded local experiments use Qwen3.8-27B BF16, two A100 80GB GPUs, TP=2, concurrency 16, and 32 rollouts from 8 GSM8K questions. Each fixed-work replay has 113 model calls and 8,121 output tokens. The principal comparisons use three runs per configuration and report median throughput relative to native APC at the **same GPU KV budget**; movement additionally uses a host Store.

| GPU KV per GPU          | Configuration                 | Native / reference elapsed | Throughput change |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------: | ----------------: |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Quota/prefix-reuse scheduling |          449.06 / 219.63 s |           +104.5% |
| 2 GiB, constrained      | Retention + movement + quota  |          449.06 / 247.60 s |            +81.4% |
| 8 GiB, working set fits | Retention + movement + quota  |            54.09 / 56.13 s |             -3.6% |

These measurements support executable lifecycle/resource contracts and a scheduling benefit under constrained KV capacity. They do **not** establish an additional benefit from movement/composition over quota alone, or a general serving speedup. The 2 GiB setting is an artificial pressure diagnostic. When the working set fits, both arms have zero preemptions and equal cache hits; control overhead produces a regression.

Separate live tool runs took 452.37 / 288.73 / 214.34 s for native/full-policy/quota, each scoring 32/32 rewards. These are single runs with different generated trajectories and only 8 independent questions. Fixed replay reruns model generation but does not rerun tools or evaluate rewards.

The [experiment report](https://github.com/zhhangBian/vllm-note/blob/rfc-hint/docs/programmable-kvc/rollout-report-2026-10-12.md) records variability, tail-latency regressions, missing Store objects, methodology, and unfinished acceptance. Raw traces/logs remain local and are not included in this PR.

### Related work and remaining scope

Duplicate checks covered #57103's discussion, open PRs referencing it, and KV-hint/programmable-cache searches. [#58198](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58198) supplies a minimal request-free CPU-to-GPU primitive; [#59714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59714) and [#38514](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38514) cover retention priority. This reference has a broader purpose: a runnable control/lifecycle/resource/execution path plus policy and rollout experiments. Its overlapping primitive, dispatcher, and priority code needs consolidation with those contributions before upstream merge. The experimental COPY/MOVE schema follows the direction discussed in #59708 and remains open to revision.

This draft preserves development baseline `30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7` and currently has conflicts with upstream `main`. Rebase and validation against current `main` remain open. Other gaps include the full prediction/fairness/outage/restart matrix, a fresh final 128-question evaluation, other models/layouts, Dynamo/llm-d integration, and full RL trainer/optimizer performance. CPU control requires one block per chunk; native Mooncake movement requires PCP=DCP=1. Cold-tier retention/deletion and mixed native/backend envelopes are unsupported.

## Validation

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,3 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_control.py \
  tests/v1/test_kv_hint_state.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_control.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/kv_control/test_api.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref 30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7 --to-ref rfc-hint --show-diff-on-failure
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --from-ref 30f5c01d4ebb5c493ed86195db24d0ec5b3ce3d7 --to-ref rfc-hint
openspec validate programmable-kv-cache --strict
```

The recorded regression result is **680 passed**, with 14 PyTorch deprecation warnings. The implementation files tested are identical to those in this branch; the subsequent history edit changes attribution trailers only. The full branch pre-commit checks passed. Python 3.12 type checks and OpenSpec strict validation passed on the same implementation. The model and rollout measurements above are earlier experimental results, not newly rerun evaluations.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation, and PR preparation. The human submitter has confirmed reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant tests.

class ToolWaitPolicy(KVPolicy):
    consumed_signals = frozenset({"tool_wait", "resume", "resume_prediction"})
    signal_updates_guidance = False

    def __init__(
        self,
        tier: Literal["cpu", "mooncake"] = "mooncake",
        lead_seconds: float = 0.1,
        min_pressure: float = 0.0,
        max_stored_blocks: int = 16384,
        min_pause_seconds: float = 0.5,
        prefetch_on_admission: bool = False,
        consider_pause_duration: bool = True,
    ):
        if tier not in ("cpu", "mooncake"):
            raise ValueError("Movement policy requires CPU or Mooncake")
        if not math.isfinite(lead_seconds) or lead_seconds < 0:
            raise ValueError("lead_seconds must be nonnegative and finite")
        if not math.isfinite(min_pressure) or not 0 <= min_pressure <= 1:
            raise ValueError("min_pressure must be between zero and one")
        self.tier = tier
        self.lead_seconds = lead_seconds
        self.min_pressure = min_pressure
        if not math.isfinite(min_pause_seconds) or min_pause_seconds < 0:
            raise ValueError("min_pause_seconds must be nonnegative and finite")
        self.min_pause_seconds = min_pause_seconds
        self.prefetch_on_admission = prefetch_on_admission
        self.uses_scheduler_guidance = prefetch_on_admission
        self.consider_pause_duration = consider_pause_duration

class SessionTarget(  # type: ignore[call-arg]
    msgspec.Struct,
    tag="session",
    tag_field="kind",
    frozen=True,
    forbid_unknown_fields=True,
):
    session_id: Identifier
    continuation_id: Identifier | None = None
    start_token: TokenPosition = 0
    end_token: TokenPosition | None = None


class RequestTarget(  # type: ignore[call-arg]
    msgspec.Struct,
    tag="request",
    tag_field="kind",
    frozen=True,
    forbid_unknown_fields=True,
):
    request_id: Identifier
    start_token: TokenPosition = 0
    end_token: TokenPosition | None = None


Target: TypeAlias = HashTarget | SessionTarget | RequestTarget


class RetainPayload(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
    target: Target
    owner_id: Identifier
    declaration_id: Identifier
    priority: Annotated[int, msgspec.Meta(ge=0, le=100)] = 0
    ttl_seconds: PositiveSeconds | None = None
    tier: Tier = "gpu"
    scope: Literal["snapshot", "follow_growth"] = "snapshot"


class ReleasePayload(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
    owner_id: Identifier
    declaration_id: Identifier


class EvictPayload(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
    target: Target
    tier: Tier = "gpu"


class DemotePayload(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True, forbid_unknown_fields=True):  # type: ignore[call-arg]
    target: Target
    destination: Literal["cpu", "mooncake"]

def popleft(self) -> KVCacheBlock:
        return self.popleft_n(1)[0]

    def popleft_n(self, n: int) -> list[KVCacheBlock]:
        if n < 0 or n > self.num_free_blocks:
            raise ValueError("Not enough free blocks")
        self.last_displaced_cached_blocks = 0
        if n == 0:
            return []
        self._synchronize()
        selected: list[KVCacheBlock] = []
        while len(selected) < n:
            priority, order, block_id = heapq.heappop(self._heap)
            if self._keys.get(block_id) != (priority, order):
                continue
            block = self._all_blocks[block_id]
            super().remove(block)
            del self._keys[block_id]
            self.last_displaced_cached_blocks += block.block_hash is not None
            selected.append(block)
        self._compact()
        return selected

def test_high_priority_expiry_does_not_extend_or_delete_another_owner(
    index, declarations, now
):
    shared = span(1)
    associate(index, "a", (shared,))
    associate(index, "b", (shared,))
    retain(declarations, "a", 90, 5)
    low = retain(declarations, "b", 20, 20)
    assert declarations.priority(0, shared.block_hash) == 90
    now[0] += 5
    assert declarations.priority(0, shared.block_hash) == 20
    assert declarations.get("a", "keep") is None
    assert declarations.get("b", "keep") == low
    now[0] += 15
    assert declarations.priority(0, shared.block_hash) == 0


def test_cache_hits_and_following_growth_do_not_renew_ttl(index, declarations, now):
    initial = associate(index, "a", (span(1),))
    retained = retain(declarations, "a", 70, 5, follow=True)
    now[0] += 4
    associate(index, "hit", (span(1),))
    index.associate(
        "a", "main", (span(1), span(2, 16, 32)), expected_revision=initial.revision
    )
    assert declarations.get("a", "keep") == retained
    assert declarations.priority(0, span(2).block_hash) == 70
    now[0] += 1
    assert declarations.priority(0, span(1).block_hash) == 0
    assert declarations.priority(0, span(2).block_hash) == 0

def test_attached_priority_ttl_starts_at_completion_and_duplicate_does_not_renew():
    from vllm.v1.outputs import ModelRunnerOutput

    engine, controller, _ = primitive_scheduler()
    now = [0.0]
    copies = controller.executor.retention_priority.copies
    copies.clock = lambda: now[0]
    request = token_request("priority", [1] * 32)
    request.sampling_params.max_tokens = request.max_tokens = 1
    hint = primitive_envelope(
        "retain",
        "vllm.set_priority",
        {
            "target": "request_cached",
            "location": "local_g1",
            "claim_id": "router/task",
            "revision": 1,
            "value": -10,
            "ttl_seconds": 5,
        },
    )
    request.kv_hints = hint
    engine.add_request(request)
    scheduled = engine.scheduler.schedule()
    blocks = list(
        engine.scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_blocks(request.request_id).blocks[0]
    )
    assert all(copies.priority(b) is None for b in blocks)
    now[0] = 100
    engine.scheduler.update_from_output(
        scheduled,
        ModelRunnerOutput(
            req_ids=[request.request_id],
            req_id_to_index={request.request_id: 0},
            sampled_token_ids=[[0]],
            logprobs=None,
            prompt_logprobs_dict={},
            pooler_output=[],
        ),
    )
    assert controller.registry.get("retain", "action").status == "completed"
    assert all(copies.priority(b) == -10 for b in blocks)
    now[0] = 104
    registry = controller.registry
    replay = controller.submit(
        hint,
        ControlContext(registry.engine_id, registry.engine_epoch, "native"),
        request_id=request.request_id,
    )
    assert replay.replayed
    now[0] = 105
    copies.expire()
    assert all(copies.priority(b) is None for b in blocks)

## SET_PRIORITY

The #59714-compatible payload is:

```json
{
  "target": "request_cached",
  "location": "local_g1",
  "claim_id": "router/task-1",
  "revision": 1,
  "value": 10,
  "ttl_seconds": 60
}
```

A signed integer value sets the eviction priority of a physical cache copy.
A finite positive TTL starts when the priority takes effect.
Copies with higher effective priority are evicted later; normal free-list/LRU ordering breaks ties.
`value: null`, no TTL and a higher revision clear only this claim.
Equal/older revisions do not renew TTL; conflicting payloads at an equal revision reject the operation before changing any selected claim.
An explicit claim ends when a higher revision clears it with null, its TTL expires, or its physical copy is invalidated.
An arbitrary claim ID does not associate the claim with a logical task, so task completion cannot infer that ownership.
Task cleanup also removes the associated local-policy claims.
The controller retains the latest revision for each claim ID, including cleared claims, until the copy is invalidated, reused or reset.
This retained revision prevents stale updates from recreating a cleared claim; each copy supports at most 16 claim IDs.
Reconstructed copies do not inherit these claims.

Logical selectors are an extension selecting currently resident copies.
Legacy Retain/Release declarations retain their independent logical-content lifetimes and can follow newly appended content when configured.
Both declaration families feed **one** `RetentionFreeBlockQueue`, using the maximum valid priority; the default 0 applies only when no declaration exists.
Priority never pins memory, allocates blocks, or changes active references.

Legacy action version `1` remains supported (`retain`, `release`, `evict`, `demote`, `prefetch`, `share`, state commands and signals).
Explicit eviction has no implicit mapping to clearing priority.
Optional retention/tool-wait policies now produce version-1.0 primitives through the same execution boundary.
A SET_PRIORITY proposal waits for overlapping GPU COPY proposals from the same signal before application; its TTL starts after the copy is ready, and failed copies yield explicit missing or partial priority outcomes.
Waiting proposals do not consume the execution budget, so a one-action-per-step limit cannot starve their prerequisites.
There is no automatic tool-call detector.
Request-free control and local policy production are explicit extensions to the initial request-attached RFC profile.

Policies may declare `consumed_signals` as an immutable set of signal names.
Signals with no configured consumer return `unconsumed` without building a request observation or invalidating scheduler guidance.
The default `None` preserves delivery of every signal to existing third-party policies.
Subclasses must explicitly redeclare the filter to opt in, so an overridden handler does not silently inherit a narrower signal set.

The built-in tool-wait policy accepts `resume_after_seconds` on the initial
`tool_wait` signal. It skips a speculative round trip when that estimate does
not exceed `min_pause_seconds` (default 0.5) or its observed store-plus-load time.
`consider_pause_duration=false` selects the pressure-only ablation. Missing
estimates keep pressure-based demotion. Skipped movement history is bounded and
cleaned with its logical owners; explicit movement commands are unaffected.
This heuristic does not estimate GPU recomputation cost or guarantee residency.
In admission-coupled mode a short tool can also use a sustained GPU backlog:
current referenced occupancy must reach `min_pressure`, and an observed waiting
request must have waited longer than the minimum window or measured store/load
round trip, whichever is larger. With low current occupancy a short pause keeps
G1 content even when projected demand is high. Observed queue age is a heuristic
for this decision, not a prediction of the target request's remaining wait.

`prefetch_on_admission=true` enables scheduler coordination for the movement
policy. Under queued demand, a matching session's GPU COPY waits until that
session is selected for admission. The scheduler starts preparation before cache
lookup and waits for terminal publication; failure permits ordinary recomputation.
Without queued demand the predicted preparation may execute early. Cancellation
and task cleanup release queued scope without acquiring transfer buffers.
